cohort_context: FRAUD-VS-CONTROL DISCRIMINATION TEST. WKHS is the borderline member: at the 2021-02-01 cutoff no SEC action has been announced, but SEC ultimately settled (2024, $1.7M) over USPS-contract-related disclosures. The 10-K filed 2020-03-13 (FY2019) is the most substantive pre-cutoff filing. The framework is being asked: does multi-source aggregation, blinded to the eventual SEC settlement, surface signals consistent with the SEC's eventual view? Match-pair: RIDE (Lordstown Motors) on the EV-truck SPAC narrative. The 10-K explicitly discloses (a) the LMC/Lordstown Motors license transaction founded by a former Workhorse CEO, (b) the USPS NGDV prototype + RFP-in-progress posture, (c) going-concern qualifier with accumulated deficit $178.8M, (d) Marathon secured-credit-cluster financings. Each is independently testable against the catalog.

claims.claim_text: Workhorse was one of five participants selected by the United States Postal Service (USPS) to build prototype vehicles for the USPS Next Generation Delivery Vehicle (NGDV) project, delivered six prototype vehicles in September 2017 under a USPS prototype contract, and the USPS published a Request for Proposals in December 2019 for the Production Program.
claims.source_quote: Workhorse was one of the five participants that the United States Postal Service ( USPS ) selected to build prototype vehicles for the USPS Next Generation Delivery Vehicle ( NGDV ) project. The USPS has publicly stated that approximately 165,000 vehicles are to be replaced. In September 2017, Workhorse delivered six vehicles for prototype testing under the NGDV Acquisition Program in compliance with the terms set forth in their USPS prototype contract. In 2019, the vehicles completed the required testing protocol as specified by the USPS. The USPS published a Request for Proposals in December 2019 for the Production Program.
claims.subject: Workhorse Group Inc.
claims.object_value: USPS NGDV; 6 prototype vehicles delivered Sept 2017; RFP published Dec 2019

creative_extensions.source_label: USPS Office of Inspector General audit reports + USPS NGDV RFP records
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.uspsoig.gov/document-library + USPS NGDV public RFP/SAM.gov solicitation history (Solicitation 6CAPSU-16-B-0007 family)
creative_extensions.rationale: USPS does not buy through GSA/USAspending the way DoD/civil agencies do; USPS prototype contracts are administered internally. The OIG audit library and USPS-administered solicitation records are the canonical adjudicator for NGDV prototype-participant identity and contract scope.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: list of NGDV prototype awardees; contract values; modification history
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if WKHS is named as one of the 5 NGDV prototype awardees: corroborates; if absent or mis-scoped (e.g. listed as subcontractor only): contradicts the framing

creative_extensions.source_label: GAO reports on USPS vehicle modernization
creative_extensions.rationale: GAO has tracked the NGDV program; reports name prototype awardees and discuss program status. Would corroborate whether WKHS was actually one of the 5 prototype participants.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: named-awardee list; program-status descriptions
creative_extensions.signal_direction: WKHS-named corroborates; absent contradicts

creative_extensions.source_label: Counterparty SEC fulltext (USPS does not file with SEC; check NGDV co-bidders Oshkosh/Karsan-Morgan Olson/AM General/VT Hackney/Mahindra references)
creative_extensions.rationale: Oshkosh (the eventual NGDV awardee, post-cutoff knowledge but pre-cutoff a public bidder candidate) and other public co-bidders may reference NGDV competitive set in their pre-cutoff filings.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: filings naming the NGDV prototype-awardee cohort
creative_extensions.signal_direction: co-bidder filings naming Workhorse corroborate; absence is non-informative

claims.extraction_notes: This is the CENTRAL claim. The eventual 2024 SEC settlement concerned WKHS's disclosures about its USPS-contract prospects. At cutoff, the prototype contract itself is real but the production-award outcome is unknown. usaspending.query_federal_presence will likely show LOW or ZERO USPS contracts (USPS is largely outside USAspending coverage), so an INFLATION_SUSPECT signal here is NOT a contradiction by itself — it is a coverage limitation. The creative-extension OIG/GAO/SAM-solicitation pathway is the actually-canonical test. Mark this carefully — false positive risk if the framework treats USPS absence in USAspending as hard contradiction.

claims.claim_text: Workhorse has received six separate orders totaling up to 1,405 vehicles from UPS under a Vehicle Purchase Agreement dated June 4, 2014; the sixth and most recent order is from Q1 2018.
claims.source_quote: On June 4, 2014, the Company entered into a Vehicle Purchase Agreement with United Parcel Service Inc. ( UPS ) which outlined the relationship by which the Company would sell vehicles to UPS. To date, we have received six separate orders totaling up to 1,405 vehicles from UPS. The sixth and most recent order is from the first quarter of 2018.
claims.subject: Workhorse Group Inc.
claims.object_value: UPS; 6 orders totaling up to 1,405 vehicles; latest Q1 2018

creative_extensions.source_label: UPS 10-K / 10-Q fulltext via EDGAR (CIK 0001090727)
creative_extensions.rationale: Per H7 calibration, mega-cap fleet operators (UPS is mid-large cap, ~$120B) rarely disclose sub-material small-cap suppliers. But 1,405 vehicles at WKHS pricing is sub-material to UPS revenue — absence would be expected, not contradictory. Test anyway for context.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of UPS filings mentioning 'Workhorse'
creative_extensions.signal_direction: absent = baseline / non-informative; present = strong corroboration; ZERO mentions over 6+ years of orders would be informative absence given the 1,405-vehicle headline

creative_extensions.source_label: UPS press releases + UPS sustainability reports archive
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://about.ups.com/us/en/newsroom + UPS annual Sustainability Report PDFs
creative_extensions.rationale: UPS publicizes EV-fleet milestones in sustainability comms. 1,405-vehicle Workhorse order would plausibly appear in UPS press around 2018-2019 if active.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: press references; fleet-electrification milestone counts
creative_extensions.signal_direction: named milestone = corroborates; silence post-2018 corroborates the cooling-relationship subtext

claims.extraction_notes: UPS is a mega-cap counterparty (~$120B mcap). H7 caution applies — UPS 10-K unlikely to disclose a sub-0.5% supplier. The materiality-correct test is claim_evolution: does WKHS keep re-disclosing the UPS order book in subsequent 10-Qs/8-Ks through 2020? If 'silent post claim,' that is a soft distress / order-cancellation signal. Latest order being Q1 2018 (i.e. ~2 years stale by 10-K filing) is itself a quiet caution flag the framework should encode.

claims.claim_text: Workhorse has built and delivered approximately 360 electric and range-extended medium-duty delivery trucks cumulatively, and is the only American commercial electric vehicle OEM to achieve such a milestone, to its knowledge.
claims.source_quote: Workhorse delivery trucks are produced at our Union City, Indiana plant and are in use by our customers on daily routes across the United States. To date, we have built and delivered approximately 360 electric and range extended medium-duty delivery trucks to our customers. To our knowledge, we are the only American commercial electric vehicle OEM to achieve such a milestone.
claims.subject: Workhorse Group Inc.

creative_extensions.source_label: NHTSA vPIC VIN decoder + IIHS Highway Loss Data Institute registrations
creative_extensions.rationale: NHTSA vPIC registers every U.S. vehicle manufacturer with vehicle type classification ('Truck' vs 'Incomplete Vehicle'). A claimed 360 cumulative deliveries of medium-duty trucks implies ~360 WMI-registered VINs over 2015-2019. Currently NHTSA returns the manufacturer record but not per-year VIN counts — proposed extension would query IIHS HLDI for registration counts.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of WKHS-WMI VINs registered by year; vehicle type
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if registered count << 360 cumulative: contradicts production claim; if 'Incomplete Vehicle' rather than 'Truck': contradicts OEM framing

creative_extensions.source_label: EPA Vehicle Certification database
creative_extensions.rationale: EPA certifies every model-year of every road vehicle sold in the US. A 6-year history of EV-truck deliveries should appear as Workhorse-certified medium-duty model-year filings.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: certified model-years by manufacturer; engine family designations
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence of multiple model-year certifications corroborates ongoing OEM; absence contradicts

creative_extensions.source_label: CARB (California Air Resources Board) HVIP voucher records
creative_extensions.rationale: CARB's Hybrid and Zero-Emission Truck Voucher Incentive Project (HVIP) lists every eligible electric truck by VIN; many WKHS deliveries plausibly used HVIP vouchers. A 360-unit cumulative delivery should leave a HVIP redemption trail.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: voucher-redemption counts per manufacturer; eligible-vehicle catalog entries
creative_extensions.signal_direction: voucher count << claim contradicts; matching count corroborates

claims.extraction_notes: Per taxonomy, production_count for autos_vehicles is PROVISIONAL with nhtsa as primary. The taxonomy explicitly notes 'Incomplete Vehicle = chassis/glider only, NOT a true OEM' — this is the discriminator. Workhorse Custom Chassis history (the company sold its chassis business to AMP Trucks in 2013 per 10-K Exhibit 10.1) raises the question of whether current WKHS is registered as full-OEM or Incomplete Vehicle in vPIC. NHTSA-as-Incomplete with a 360-truck claim would be a soft mismatch.

claims.claim_text: Workhorse owns a 250,000 square-foot truck assembly facility on 47 acres in Union City, Indiana with capacity to build up to 60,000 trucks per year, plus a 45,000 sq ft administration/R&D/manufacturing facility in Loveland, Ohio.
claims.source_quote: Our truck assembly facility is located in Union City, Indiana. This facility consists of three buildings with 250,000 square feet of manufacturing and office space on 47 acres. This plant has capacity to build up to 60,000 trucks per year. ... Our company headquarters and 45,000 sq. ft. research and development facility is located at 100 Commerce Drive, Loveland, Ohio, a Cincinnati suburb.
claims.subject: Workhorse Group Inc.
claims.object_value: Union City, IN (250k sqft, 60,000 trucks/yr capacity); Loveland, OH (45k sqft HQ/R&D)

creative_extensions.source_label: OSHA Form 300A Establishment Search at the Union City and Loveland addresses
creative_extensions.rationale: A 250,000 sq ft assembly plant with stated 60,000 truck/yr capacity implies a headcount far above the OSHA 300A 20-emp filing threshold. Absence at Union City would be a CLAIMED_LOCATION_GAP equivalent for industrial scale. (Note: WKHS later disclosed Union City had only ~100 employees in 2020 — a real plant but operating at a small fraction of stated capacity.)
creative_extensions.expected_observable: establishment records, annual_average_employees, NAICS code
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence with low headcount (<200) = real-but-undersubscribed plant; absence = stronger contradiction; presence at Loveland but NOT Union City = HQ-only scope

creative_extensions.source_label: BLS QCEW Randolph County IN (FIPS 18135) NAICS 3361 employment baseline
creative_extensions.rationale: 60,000 trucks/yr is a stated CAPACITY (not delivery count). A facility actually operating at that scale would dominate Randolph County NAICS 3361 employment (population ~25k). Even at 10% utilization (i.e. 6,000 trucks/yr) the employment footprint would be ~500-1000 FTE — a plurality of the county's manufacturing workforce. QCEW data adjudicates the plausibility of the OPERATIONAL scale, separate from the legal-CAPACITY claim.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: county+NAICS employment denominator
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if claimed scale would represent <2% of county NAICS-3361 employment, capacity is dormant; >50% means real

creative_extensions.source_label: Randolph County Indiana property tax assessor + Union City utility/water-tap records
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: county-assessor portal (manual) + Indiana state environmental permit database
creative_extensions.rationale: A 47-acre, 250,000 sqft owned assembly facility leaves a property-tax and state-environmental-permit footprint that is independent of EPA federal registries.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: parcel ownership; assessed value; air/water permit holder
creative_extensions.signal_direction: ownership match = corroborates physical existence (not operating scale); state permits = operational

claims.extraction_notes: Per taxonomy, facility_scope for autos_vehicles is PROVISIONAL with EPA + OSHA primary. Vehicle assembly DOES involve paint/solvents -> EPA permits expected. The '60,000 trucks/yr capacity' claim is the operational-scale-fingerprint test (per the OPERATIONAL CAPACITY TESTING section) — even a real plant operating at 1% utilization would not generate the EPA TRI/GHGRP footprint of a real Class 3-6 truck OEM. This is the test that most distinguishes a real OEM from a glider-only operation.

claims.claim_text: Workhorse's 2019 financial statements include a going-concern qualifier; the Company had an accumulated deficit of $178.8 million as of December 31, 2019, current liabilities exceeded current assets by $15.5M, total liabilities exceeded total assets by $34.9M, and 2019 net cash used in operating activities was $36.9M; the Company has no committed future funding.
claims.source_quote: As discussed in Note 1 to the financial statements, the Company incurred a net loss of $37,162,827 during the year ended December 31, 2019, and as of that date, the Company s current liabilities exceeded its current assets by $15,524,360 and its total liabilities exceeded its total assets by $34,913,110. These conditions, along with other matters as set forth in Note 1, raise substantial doubt about the Company s ability to continue as a going concern. ... We have an accumulated deficit of $178.8 million as of December 31, 2019. ... We expect to have adequate capital to continue operations through the second quarter 2020.
claims.subject: Workhorse Group Inc.
claims.object_value: going-concern qualifier; accumulated deficit $178.8M; stockholders' deficit $34.9M; negative working capital $15.5M; cash runway Q2 2020

creative_extensions.source_label: claim_evolution self-disclosure tracking on 'going concern' language
creative_extensions.rationale: Distress-cluster fingerprints are temporal. Tracking whether 'going concern' language persists, intensifies, or disappears in 2020 10-Qs and subsequent 10-K filings is the canonical adjudicator of distress evolution.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of filings mentioning going-concern; covenant references; subsequent-event disclosures
creative_extensions.signal_direction: persistent language = chronic distress; disappearance = resolved (often via dilutive equity raise — which is itself a distress marker)

creative_extensions.source_label: SEC EDGAR S-3/S-1/424B prospectus supplement cadence
creative_extensions.rationale: Shelf-registration draw-downs and ATM cadence are the operational fingerprint of micro-cap distress refinancing. 2019 alone shows Convertible Note $39M + Series B Pfd $25M + common $5.9M issuance — a textbook distress-cluster fingerprint per H10.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of prospectus supplements; dollar amounts raised; pace acceleration
creative_extensions.signal_direction: 3+ supplements in <12mo = elevated; pace acceleration = severe

creative_extensions.source_label: Marathon Asset Management lender concentration via SEC filings + UCC-1 Indiana/Ohio Secretary of State
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: ucc_proxy + state UCC search at IN/OH SoS
creative_extensions.rationale: The 10-K Exhibit 10.19 discloses a Marathon-led credit agreement with security agreements pledging Workhorse Technologies, Workhorse Properties, Workhorse Motor Works, Surefly — a textbook secured-distress-debt cluster. State UCC filings would directly corroborate the lien perfection events.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: UCC-1 filings; secured-creditor identity; collateral description
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence of Marathon-anchored UCC-1s corroborates the secured-distress-cluster classification

claims.extraction_notes: Per H10, multiple distress markers cluster here within a short window: going-concern qualifier + accumulated deficit + stockholders' deficit + negative working capital + secured-credit cluster (Marathon, Arosa) + 2019 convertible-note + Series B Preferred issuance + sale of SureFly division + LMC license-out (asset-light pivot). This is a real-distress cluster — exactly the operational profile where ucc_proxy + claim_evolution should fire together.

claims.claim_text: Workhorse granted Lordstown Motors Corp (LMC), founded by former Workhorse CEO Stephen S. Burns, a perpetual worldwide license to its W-15 electric pickup truck intellectual property on November 7, 2019, in exchange for a 10% ownership interest in LMC (fair value $12.2M), a minimum royalty of 1% of LMC's capital raise, and a 1% royalty on the first 200,000 LMC vehicles sold; Workhorse also intends to transfer approximately 6,000 existing Vehicle orders to LMC upon completion of LMC's Capital Raise.
claims.source_quote: On November 7, 2019, the Company entered into a transaction with LMC pursuant to which the Company granted LMC a perpetual and worldwide license to certain intellectual property relating to the Company s W-15 electric pickup truck platform and its related technology ... LMC was founded by Stephen S. Burns, a current stockholder and former Chief Executive Officer and Director of the Company. ... A ten percent ownership interest in the common stock of LMC ... One percent of the aggregate debt and equity commitments funded to LMC upon completion of the Capital Raise (the Minimum Royalty ). ... A one percent royalty on the gross sales price of the first 200,000 Vehicles sold ... Upon completion of the Capital Raise, the Company intends to transfer approximately 6,000 existing Vehicles orders to LMC.
claims.subject: Workhorse Group Inc.
claims.object_value: Lordstown Motors Corp (LMC); 10% equity; 1% minimum royalty; 1% royalty on first 200k vehicles; ~6,000 vehicle orders to be transferred

creative_extensions.source_label: Lordstown Motors / DiamondPeak Holdings DPCM S-4 / 8-K filings (CIK to be resolved; DiamondPeak SPAC merger Aug 2020)
creative_extensions.rationale: LMC merged with DiamondPeak Holdings SPAC in Aug 2020 and became public (NASDAQ: RIDE) pre-cutoff. The S-4 proxy statement is required to disclose the WKHS license, equity stake, royalty structure, and the 6,000-vehicle order transfer — all directly contradiction-testable.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: S-4 and subsequent 10-K disclosures naming Workhorse, the 10% equity grant, and the 6,000-order transfer
creative_extensions.signal_direction: matching disclosures = corroborates structure; mismatched economics or no mention = contradicts; LMC also disclosing concerns about the 6,000-order book quality would be informative

creative_extensions.source_label: USPTO patent assignment records (Workhorse -> LMC W-15 platform IP)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: uspto_odp.query_assignee + USPTO assignment search at https://assignment.uspto.gov/patent/
creative_extensions.rationale: A perpetual worldwide license of a vehicle-platform technology should leave an assignment-record or license-record trail at USPTO (assignments are voluntarily recorded but licenses sometimes are, especially when collateral or covenants attach).
creative_extensions.expected_observable: recorded assignment / license; assignor / assignee identities; effective date
creative_extensions.signal_direction: recorded license corroborates; absent is non-informative (licenses aren't mandatorily recorded)

creative_extensions.source_label: GM Lordstown Assembly Complex divestiture records + Mahoning County OH property records
creative_extensions.rationale: The LMC business plan rests on acquiring + restarting the Lordstown Assembly Complex from GM. Property records adjudicate whether LMC actually acquired the plant by cutoff, which would corroborate the operational basis of the 6,000-order transferability.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: plant ownership; purchase date; purchase price
creative_extensions.signal_direction: transfer-on-record by cutoff = corroborates; not transferred = capital-raise-contingent claim still inchoate

claims.extraction_notes: This claim has dual character: (a) a real, completed IP-license transaction (the 10% equity grant is booked as $12.2M in Other Income for FY2019 — i.e. WKHS has effectively pivoted away from W-15 pickup production into a royalty-and-equity play); and (b) a forward-looking ~6,000-vehicle order transfer that is contingent on LMC's capital raise. claim_evolution tracking the LMC story through WKHS's 2020 10-Qs adjudicates whether the relationship and order-book transfer evolved as described. RELATED-PARTY pattern: the LMC counterparty was founded by Workhorse's former CEO — a flag for the framework to weight more carefully.

claims.claim_text: Workhorse holds a patent on its HorseFly Unmanned Aerial System, has flown over 100 missions in the National Airspace System demonstrating package delivery for large multi-national companies including UPS, and sold two HorseFly systems to Unmanned Systems Operations Group (USOG) which operates them under FAA Part 107.
claims.source_quote: Workhorse was granted a patent on our UAS with the description Package Delivery by Means of an Automated Multi-Copter UAS/UAV Dispatched From A Conventional Delivery Vehicle. ... In tests and demonstrations over the past two years, Workhorse has flown over 100 missions in the National Airspace System, demonstrating package delivery for large multi-national companies, including UPS. ... Workhorse successfully delivered two of its HorseFly systems for commercial use, selling the systems to the Unmanned Systems Operations Group ("USOG"). ... USOG is using our HorseFly system and aircraft in commercial operations under Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA") regulations Part 107.
claims.subject: Workhorse Group Inc.
claims.object_value: HorseFly UAS; 1+ granted patent; 100+ NAS missions; 2 systems sold to USOG; USOG operates under FAA Part 107

creative_extensions.source_label: FAA UAS Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate registry + FAA Section 333/Part 107 waiver records
creative_extensions.rationale: USOG's operation of HorseFly under Part 107 is publicly recordable — Part 107 commercial-operator authorizations and waivers (for beyond-VLOS or rural-delivery) are FOIA-searchable. Adjudicates whether USOG is a real Part 107 operator.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: USOG Part 107 registration; waiver filings; HorseFly N-numbers
creative_extensions.signal_direction: USOG registered with HorseFly aircraft = corroborates; not registered = contradicts commercial-deployment framing

creative_extensions.source_label: FAA Aircraft Registry (N-number search for HorseFly airframes)
creative_extensions.rationale: If 2 systems sold for commercial use and 100+ NAS missions flown, the HorseFly airframes should be N-numbered (or operating under a properly-issued exemption). Manufacturer search adjudicates count of registered units.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: N-numbers registered as 'Workhorse' or 'HorseFly' manufacturer
creative_extensions.signal_direction: matching count corroborates; zero would contradict — but UAS under 55 lbs may operate without N-number, so absence is moderately informative

creative_extensions.source_label: Moog Inc 10-K disclosures of Certus JV (CIK 0000067887)
creative_extensions.rationale: The HorseFly assets were contributed to a 50/50 JV with Moog (Certus Unmanned Aerial Systems LLC) in Nov 2019 per 10-K Exhibit 10.40. Moog is a public co (NYSE: MOG.A) and must disclose JV equity-method investments in its own 10-K. This is the counterparty-disclosure test for the Moog/Certus partnership claim.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: Moog 10-K mention of Certus JV or Workhorse
creative_extensions.signal_direction: Moog disclosure of Certus / Workhorse corroborates; absence at Moog's mid-cap size where JVs ARE typically disclosed = contradictory

claims.extraction_notes: Dual-domain claim: drone IP (aviation_drones) + WKHS auto domain. Per taxonomy, patents_ip is CANONICAL with USPTO primary. Test will confirm whether WKHS holds the named UAS-multicopter patent. Note that the HorseFly assets were transferred to Certus JV (50/50 with Moog) in Nov 2019, so post-transfer the IP may be held by Certus, not WKHS directly — a subtle assignee-name question that the framework should not penalize as 'absence'.
